prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1084; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim received by phone from the insured reporting a low-speed head-on collision at an intersection. Insured states the other vehicle crossed the centerline during a turn. Both vehicles driven from scene. Police report requested. Photos of both vehicles uploaded to file.

Entry 2: Recorded statement taken from insured. Insured reports mild neck stiffness the following morning and has scheduled a visit with a physician. Vehicle inspection assigned to a field appraiser. Liability appears probable against the other driver, pending police report review.

Entry 3: Notice of representation received from claimant's attorney's office. All further contact to be directed to counsel. Medical authorization and records request sent to counsel. Claimant's treatment described as a neck strain with physical therapy recommended. No surgical recommendation at this time.

Entry 4: Appraisal received on both vehicles. Damage consistent with low-speed impact, primarily to front bumper assemblies, headlamp housings, and hood. Repair estimates reviewed and within expected range for the damage described. Rental coverage confirmed for the insured while the vehicle is in repair.

Entry 5: Demand package received from claimant's counsel including treatment notes and billing summary. File referred to supervisor for evaluation of the bodily injury component. Reserve reviewed and adjusted to reflect current treatment status. Follow-up scheduled to confirm completion of physical therapy and receipt of final records.
